routes.serves: note list JSON that feeds the home page notes area (pinned notes and regular notes)
create a note from the Take a note editor (title + content); returns 201 with the created note, 400 on invalid JSON body
soft-delete a note by id (sets deletedAt so it leaves the main notes list and lands in Trash); returns 200 with the deleted note, 404 when the id does not exist
restore a soft-deleted note by id (clears deletedAt so it returns to the main notes list); returns 200 with the restored note, 404 when the id does not exist
permanently remove a trashed note by id (used by the Delete forever action in the Trash view); returns 200 with the removed note, 404 when the id does not exist
empty the trash: permanently remove every soft-deleted note; returns 200 with the number of notes removed

notes: REQ-2.3.3: Trash list. The Trash view already exists (REQ-2.3.1 rendered deleted notes with Restore/Delete forever actions). This node adds: (1) an 'Empty trash' button shown only in the Trash view that calls the new DELETE /api/trash route (permanently removes every soft-deleted note) and then reloads the list; (2) a dedicated DELETE /api/notes/:id/forever route for the per-note 'Delete forever' action so the existing DELETE /api/notes/:id stays a soft delete (REQ-2.3.1 contract untouched); (3) automatic deletion after seven days: purgeExpiredTrash() runs on server start and on every request, permanently removing notes whose deletedAt is older than 7 days (7*24*60*60*1000 ms) before serving responses; (4) seed data: a deletable regular note titled 'Delete me 2.3.3' (content 'Temporary note for deletion flow', unpinned, not archived, not deleted) in backend/data/db.json so the acceptance flow (delete on home page -> open Trash -> note visible) works. Accessible names: 'Trash' sidebar button (existing), 'Empty trash' button (new), 'Delete Note' menuitem (existing). No new dependency on REQ-2.3.2 behavior; restore endpoint reused.
